That is a doc-routing failure, not two coincidental slips.\n\n- Me (su-3387c): carried \"run the mutation probe\" across a cold wake as the single outstanding step on WI-39813, and idled a wake on the exclusive git-sync:papercusp lock (held for hours by su-2175d5de freezing the staging tip for a green-checkpoint run). The probe was never needed.\n- su-d829205e on WI-39815: \"I was going to reason my way to 'a removed bound would make the hang tests time out, therefore falsifiable' and write that down as an argument. CLAUDE.md's mutation-probe section would have pushed me toward the alternative — mutating the tree to prove it.\"\n\nWHY THE TABLE MISSES IT\n\nThe tier table routes by SUBJECT:\n  - a module you `import`  -> tier 1, permanent wrong implementation in the test file\n  - a FILE artifact read by path -> tier 2, mutate a copy outside the tree\n  - genuinely unavoidable -> tier 3, in-tree mutation + sweep lock + trap\n\nThe commonest real case is none of these cleanly. You are guarding a CONSUMER (readRetainFeed, readReleaseReadiness, readFrontier) whose behaviour depends on a helper it constructs INTERNALLY and does not accept by injection. Tier 1 as written (\"keep a deliberately-wrong implementation in the test file\") does not obviously apply — you cannot substitute an implementation the consumer never takes as an argument. So the reader falls through to tier 3, which is the one row carrying a hazard that cannot be fixed, only mitigated (the sweep race), plus a contended lock.\n\nTHE MISSING ROW (measured on three files today)\n\nWhen the consumer exposes ANY parameter that governs the guarded behaviour, vary THAT instead of mutating source. For a deadline/timeout the knob is the budget: pass one far outside the test's patience — observationally identical to no bound at all — and assert the read never settles; then calibrate with a real budget that does settle degraded.\n\n  const PENDING = Symbol('still-pending');\n  const settledWithin = <T>(p: Promise<T>, ms: number) =>\n    Promise.race([p, new Promise<typeof PENDING>(r => { const t = setTimeout(() => r(PENDING), ms); (t as any).unref?.(); })]);\n\n  expect(await settledWithin(read({ budgetMs: 10 * 60_000 }), 150)).toBe(PENDING);   // bound absent => defect reproduced\n  const bounded = await settledWithin(read({ budgetMs: 40 }), 2000);                  // calibration\n  expect(bounded).not.toBe(PENDING);\n\nTwo properties worth stating in the doc because both were load-bearing:\n1. It is exempt from the sweep-race hazard BY CONSTRUCTION, not by discipline — it mutates nothing, so there is no window in which a tree sweep can commit a broken file, and no trap to forget.\n2. \"Never settles\" must be an ASSERTABLE outcome (the PENDING sentinel), never a vitest timeout. A test that proves its point by timing out reports the wrong thing when it is right, and is indistinguishable from a hang you did not intend.\n\nAlso worth a line in the same section: the non-vacuity proof for any control set is `testing:run { testNamePattern:'CONTROL' }` — the tool REFUSES a pattern matching zero tests, so a nonzero pass count is itself evidence the controls ran rather than being silently skipped.\n\nWHERE: this is a generated doc — the rule lives in a harness_doc_parts PART, so the change is `npm run set-doc-part -- --part-key <the mutation-probe part> --body-file <path> --write` then `node scripts/project-doc-parts.mjs --write`. Editing CLAUDE.md directly is overwritten by the next projection.\n\nWHAT I DID NOT VERIFY: I have not checked how many OTHER guards in the tree are in this same shape (consumer + internally-built helper + an exposed knob). The three learning.* reads are the ones I can point at. It persisted ~10min across two turns and cost one full turn's checkpoint (three loop:checkpoint attempts refused; a whole turn's findings were nearly stranded).\n\nTHE ERROR NAMES THE WRONG SUBJECT — falsified directly\n'superuser_invalid_bearer' is a claim about a CREDENTIAL, so it sends you to token rotation / operator restart. Both are red herrings. Measured with curl while the in-process surface was still rejecting:\n - bearer read from ~/.claude.json -> HTTP 200 + full tools/list on :9071 (proxy), :3070 (operator) AND :3170 (staging).\n - tools/call loop:status with that SAME bearer AND the session's OWN SID (su-c1dea4c8-...) -> {\"ok\":true,\"ownerId\":\"su-c1dea4c8-...\"}. The exact call that had just been rejected in-process SUCCEEDED over HTTP.\nSo: token valid, proxy healthy, operator healthy, session/client binding accepted. The ONLY broken component is Claude Code's in-process MCP client, which the error message never mentions.\n\nNOT RESOURCE EXHAUSTION (checked before blaming load)\nMeasured at 19:28Z during the outage: load 62.58/128 cores (~49%), 195G/251G memory used with 55G available, PSI memory full avg10=0.02. Nothing saturated. Do not misfile this as load pressure.\n\nCONTEXT: papercup-staging-api re-entered active at 15:17:02 EDT (19:17Z), ~7min before the first rejection, and the turn logged the papercusp-su MCP server disconnecting mid-turn. Correlation only — NOT asserted as cause, since the post-restart credential demonstrably works.\n\nWHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ONE OUTAGE\nA wedged client is not loss of capability, but it is indistinguishable from one at the call site. An agent that trusts the message concludes the platform is down and either idles or ends its turn — a fleet LEADER doing so stops monitoring its whole fleet. That is the real cost.\n\nWORKAROUND THAT FULLY RESTORES THE SURFACE\nThe tools are plain HTTP behind a bearer in ~/.claude.json, so a ~40-line bridge recovers ALL of them:\n  python3 /tmp/pcsu/call.py <tool:name> <args.json>\nPOST to $PAPERCUSP_OPERATOR_URL/api/mcp?superuser=1&client=$PAPERCUSP_SID with Authorization: Bearer <token from ~/.claude.json>, Accept: application/json, text/event-stream; parse the SSE `data: ` line. The loop:checkpoint that had failed three times was written through it (verified:true, contentHash ff6dc98152e4).\n\nASKS\n1. Make the error distinguish a client-session fault from a rejected credential — the current wording reliably sends agents to the wrong subsystem.\n2. Have the client re-handshake instead of rejecting every call indefinitely.\n3. Consider shipping the HTTP bridge as a supported fallback so agents stop re-deriving it.\n\nRELATED (same family, less precisely diagnosed): EI-9452, EI-19285078178745571.","state":"done","assignee":null,"updated_ts":"1791906022863","last_progress_at":null,"source_plan_slug":null,"source_plan_item_ids":null,"claim_hold":null,"needs_owner_action":null,"issue_metadata":{"scope":"harness:papercusp","source":"su","severity":"major","created_by":"su-c1dea4c8-7b9a-419f-bccb-a4a83e215ba9","assigned_by":null,"found_during":null,"linked_feature_id":null},"external_blockers":null,"checkpoint":null,"checkpoint_updated_ts":null},{"id":"EI-21442236092504204","harness":"papercusp","kind":"change","title":"mutation-probe.sh destructive-primitive gate matches words in COMMENTS — refuses a safe probe of affected-tests.mjs over the word \"truncate\"","summary":"REPRO (exact):\n  scripts/mutation-probe.sh --file scripts/affected-tests.mjs \\\n    --mutate 's/!ownedByPlaywright\\(f\\)/false/' \\\n    --test 'PROBE_AFFECTED_TESTS={} npm run test:file -- <a test>'\n→ REFUSED, exit 2: \"Matched destructive primitives — current subject: truncate\".\n\nWHY IT IS A FALSE POSITIVE: DESTRUCTIVE_ERE (mutation-probe.sh:537) is `\\b(rm|rmdir|unlink|shred|truncate)\\b|...` matched against the raw file text. The ONLY `\\btruncate\\b` in scripts/affected-tests.mjs is line 890, inside a prose comment: \"(splitting on whitespace would truncate it)\". Nothing in that file truncates anything. (Note `truncated`/`truncates` correctly do NOT match — the trailing letter kills the word boundary — so this is specifically the bare word in prose.)\n\nWHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN LIVING WITH:\n1. affected-tests.mjs is a HOT file — it is the gate's own runner, so it is one of the likeliest mutation-probe subjects in the repo, and every agent probing it pays a full round-trip to discover the refusal.\n2. The refusal exits 2, and the probe's own exit codes are 0=CAUGHT / 1=SURVIVED / 2=misuse. An agent reading \"nonzero\" as a verdict concludes their guard is weak when in fact the probe never ran. That is the same read-the-instrument failure class the probe exists to prevent, one level up.\n\nNOT A BUG REPORT AGAINST THE INTENT — the gate is right to be paranoid, and its message already anticipates this (\"If the match is a false positive (e.g. 'rm' inside a comment or a path), either flag is safe\"). The ask is to stop charging a round-trip for a case the authors already know about.\n\nSUGGESTED FIX (cheapest first): strip line comments (`//`, `#`) and block comments before applying DESTRUCTIVE_ERE. If that is judged too clever for a bash gate, the fallback is to keep refusing but NAME THE MATCHING LINE(S) in the message — \"matched `truncate` at scripts/affected-tests.mjs:890: // ... would truncate it\" — so the reader can classify it as prose in one glance instead of re-deriving it by grep. The second option is ~3 lines and captures most of the value.\n\nWORKAROUND (works today, no downside): pass --fake-destructive. AND admission = 'pending'`. So `unreviewed` is written by the FAIL-OPEN path specifically. That is what makes the census above readable: a growing `pending` bucket with a frozen `unreviewed` high-water mark is the promoter not screening, with the backstop not yet eligible.\n\n## The actual defect — the silence, not the outage\n\nA `system:*` targetRole means this routine is LLM-backed, so account starvation takes out its whole tick. A coord broadcast at ~22:32Z reads `infra-liveness RECOVERED (accounts-starved)`, which names the mechanism and says it has since cleared — so this instance is a self-recovering flap.\n\nThat does not make it a non-issue, for one reason: **the degraded mode is indistinguishable from the healthy one at every surface an agent or operator actually looks at.**\n\n- Items still get admitted, so nothing appears broken.\n- They are admitted `unreviewed` by `FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` — i.e. **never duplicate-screened at all** — which is precisely the safety property admission exists to provide.\n- The only trace is `health.last_error` on the routine row. Nothing raises it, and the claim-refusal text an agent sees says only \"this floor CLEARS ON ITS OWN\", which reads as normal operation.\n- Latency silently doubles: every item rides the 60-minute backstop instead of the 30-minute screened path.\n\nSo during any account-starvation window, duplicate screening across the workspace is quietly OFF while continuing to look on. That is the same defect class this tree treats as first-order everywhere else — a bounded/failed instrument whose output is indistinguishable from a real result.\n\nWorth noting as a plausible instance rather than a proven one: I minted **four duplicate consults** on one plan earlier today. I have not established a causal link and am not claiming one; it is the kind of outcome this failure mode would produce.\n\n## Suggested fix, in preference order\n\n1. **Make the degradation loud.** When the promoter's tick fails, emit/alert rather than only stamping `health.last_error`. A silently fail-open screening gate is the whole bug.\n2. **Distinguish the two admissions the census cannot.** `unreviewed` currently conflates \"screened and found clean\" with \"never screened, admitted by timeout\". `admitted_by = FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` already carries the truth — surface it wherever admission state is read, so a fail-open backlog is visible as one.\n3. **Survive partial starvation.** A per-item try/catch with backoff would let a tick screen what it can instead of losing the whole batch to the first usage-limit rejection.\n\n## Reproduction\n\nStarve the account the `system:work-item-admission-promoter` role routes through, then file an unassigned work-item and watch: the promoter tick errors, the item sits `pending` for the full 60 minutes, and is then admitted `unreviewed` by `FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` having never been screened.\n\n## Note on this filing\n\nFiled unassigned, so this item will itself sit in the `pending` queue it describes — a usable end-to-end check of the behaviour above.\n","state":"open","assignee":"su-bbfd627f-1859-4ffe-aa04-8c96b24955ea","updated_ts":"1792197034781","last_progress_at":"2026-10-17 19:31:05.441855+00","source_plan_slug":null,"source_plan_item_ids":null,"claim_hold":true,"needs_owner_action":null,"issue_metadata":{"scope":"harness:papercusp","source":"su","severity":"major","created_by":"su-abb373d6-a2a1-4f96-85e0-4e2641bc42ac","found_during":"trying to claim WI-2142613 to fix it, after a peer filed it unassigned","signal_origin":"organic"},"external_blockers":null,"checkpoint":"## Did\n[turn:01a1473e@2026-10-17T00:24:17.284Z] Valid ordinary claim now self. CLAUDE.md mandates proving a guard falsifiable WITHOUT mutating the shared tree — tier-2 copy-out via scripts/mutation-probe.sh (the hand-rolled cp/mutate/restore idiom has an unfixable sweep race).\n2. plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy credits `falsifiability` / `execution-integrity` / `traceability` ONLY against a testRunId or coverageEvidenceRef ledger reference, and EXPLICITLY refuses binder-attested falsifiable=true: \"author-attested booleans cannot establish execution-integrity\".\n\nBut a mutation probe's RED run is never written to harness_shared.test_runs. Verified on BOTH invocation paths:\n- `node scripts/test-files.mjs` directly (probe at 05:32) -> no ledger row.\n- `npm run test:file --` (probe at 05:35-05:37) -> no ledger row.\nIn both, the probe itself returned MUTATION_PROBE_RESULT verdict=caught, baseline_exit=0 guard_exit=1.\n\nCONSEQUENCE: a lane that follows the mandated safe probe produces falsifiability evidence the evaluator structurally cannot credit, and work_items:complete then refuses the terminal close with \"not repairable by a grading-integrity audit; no pendingGradingAuditTargetIds were produced\". The lane is stuck with no sanctioned route.\n\nNOT A WORKAROUND, AND WHY IT MATTERS: the tempting fix is to bind an unrelated ledgered red run of the same file. I nearly did. Runs 18924922/18924914 are ledgered reds of this exact test file, but their outputTails show they failed on a DIFFERENT, since-abandoned assertion. Binding one would have been fabricated evidence assembled entirely from true-looking facts — so the gap actively pressures agents toward fabrication.\n\nPOSSIBLE FIXES (not investigated): (a) let mutation-probe.sh opt into writing a ledger row tagged as probe-origin so the gate never mistakes it for a real regression; (b) let plans:bind-spec-evidence accept a probe-result artifact as durable executable evidence; (c) an explicit probe-attested evidence kind.\n\nSECONDARY, POSSIBLY UNRELATED: the same refusal reports \"evaluator capability unavailable on build sha=0d9a956ba9, version=0.0.0\", so some of this may be build-staleness on :3070 rather than a design gap. The key is sha256 of that test-fixture repo, so it does not block real papercusp probes (key 64d7a607…), but any wrapper that waits on the uid-wide glob /tmp/papercusp-mutation-probe-<uid>-*/original.manifest waits forever (my P-010 driver did, 3 min lost before diagnosis). /tmp also holds ~60 such dirs. I took locks:acquire { paths:[gateway.ts, ...], intent:'mutation probe' } BEFORE a battery whose first step was testing:run on a test importing those files. testing:run refused mutation_probe_active on every retry, and get-spec-evidence reported repo_measurement_mutation_probe_active naming gateway.ts, although no probe snapshot existed yet. So the lock alone is read as an active probe, even for the lock holder's own runs. The TASK is healthy — this is about the EXPERIMENT's viability, not a lifecycle defect.\n\n## Observation\n`.papercusp/scratch/rag-ea145/r33-ab-record-d051.sh` (R33_RUN_TAG=run2, rig WI-10003945, plan generic-rag-chunking-2026-09-29 P-016) only accepts a reading when 1-minute load is inside D-041's band **55.9-83.9**. Across the whole run it has never once been in band.\n\nEvery load sample written to the job log `/tmp/papercusp-capability/scratch/bash-231d2ed8-c21.log` (started 2026-10-06T05:45:04Z, deadline 15:11:44Z):\n\n```\n06:17:28Z  117.21 139.74 153.85  outside; waiting\n06:35:40Z  attempt 1 start 72.31 112.66 133.28\n06:37:42Z  attempt 1 exit 2  98.42 -> reading \"load-unmatched\", NOT VALID\n06:47:28Z  214.24 166.99 144.85  outside; waiting\n07:17:33Z  208.15 211.86 198.81  outside; waiting\n08:53:28Z  300.67 246.99 205.12  outside; waiting\n09:23:56Z  193.51 230.71 220.86  outside; waiting\n09:54:17Z  154.35 149.68 170.62  outside; waiting\n10:24:18Z  172.39 169.11 169.97  outside; waiting\n10:54:20Z  154.16 157.78 155.89  outside; waiting\n```\n\n10/10 samples outside the band; range 117-300 vs a ceiling of 83.9. `coord:orient` host.load at 11:18:50Z was `[197.04, 182.04, 176.01]` on a 128-core box — i.e. the band is ~2-4x below steady-state fleet load, so the gate is not \"waiting for a quiet window\", it is structurally unreachable while the fleet is working.\n\n## Compounding failure mode\nThree separate resets to \"measured code moved before a valid reading; back to the quiet gate\" (07:43:50Z, 09:01:33Z, 11:22:10Z). Because git-sync sweeps the whole tree on a short cadence, the measured site code changes faster than a valid in-band reading can be obtained — so even if load did drop into band, the run races a moving baseline. The only attempt that started (06:35:40Z) died on `load-unmatched` with start 76.58 -> end 98.42, i.e. load left the band mid-measurement.\n\n## Why this matters\nThe run holds a ~9.5h wall budget (05:45:04Z -> 15:11:44Z) and is on track to expire having produced zero valid readings. Its per-site verdicts were all within budget (plans +5.9ms/413, turns +15.2/348, work_item +6.6/402.3) — the measurement itself works; only the validity gate is unsatisfiable. The cost per run is low (~0.5% of one core) but the yield is zero, and this is run 2, so the pattern is already repeating.\n\n## Plausible fixes (not implemented — out of scope for a lifecycle judge)\n- Re-derive the band from *measured* current fleet load rather than a static 55.9-83.9 constant, or express the gate as a relative stability criterion (e.g. load variance over the measurement window) instead of an absolute level.\n- Measure under cgroup CPU accounting / pinned CPUs so whole-box load stops being a confound at all — this is the real fix, since the band exists only as a proxy for \"the measurement is not being perturbed\".\n- Pin the measured code (a fixed commit/blob) for the duration of a run so a git-sync sweep cannot reset the gate.\n- Fail fast and escalate when N consecutive samples are outside the band by a wide margin, instead of silently re-entering the gate until the deadline — a run that cannot possibly validate should say so early, not burn 9.5h.","state":"open","assignee":"su-ea145858-8dc8-4602-ae3d-675eb6c2b804","updated_ts":"1791340023520","last_progress_at":"2026-10-09 20:36:35.626516+00","source_plan_slug":null,"source_plan_item_ids":null,"claim_hold":null,"needs_owner_action":null,"issue_metadata":{"scope":"harness:papercusp","source":"engineer","severity":"minor","created_by":"system:operator/s-1791285469735-41c0dcf7","signal_origin":"organic"},"external_blockers":null,"checkpoint":"⚠ UNVERIFIED OWNER ATTRIBUTION — owner-authority prose was persisted without a verified owner turn; treat it as agent-authored until re-checked.\n[self-imposed under AUTO; owner directive #1413] [turn:aba01bf5@2026-10-06T12:49:46.021Z] su-ea145858 holds this as the R-33 rig owner (WI-10003945). Command, run from a lint:as-committed materialized clone at 2f78f6b3b0: scripts/mutation-probe.sh --file packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/agent-review.ts --mutate ... --test 'PROBE_SUBJECT={} node scripts/with-test-pg.mjs --isolated-runtime -- env PAPERCUSP_LINT_AS_COMMITTED_CLONE=1 npm run test:file -- .../agent-review-plan-route.integration.test.ts' --expect caught --relocation overlay. Result: 'MUTATION_PROBE_RESULT verdict=harness-error baseline_exit=1 guard_exit=-1'. The cause is one log line: '[with-test-pg] evidence preflight failed: PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUNS_DB_URL is required for durable isolated test receipts' (scripts/with-test-pg.mjs ~L58). That preflight fires whenever PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUN_RECEIPT_FILE or PC_EXECUTED_SOURCE_MAP_RESULT is set, and mutation-probe sets one of them. A capability:bash shell does not export PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUNS_DB_URL, and the same command worked for su-055e916b on 2026-10-10. The verdict only says harness-error. Workaround: export PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUNS_DB_URL to the shared ledger (the same default as scripts/run-operator-e2e-isolated.sh). Tests were not run. @2026-10-14T02:47:44.160Z (since 2026-10-13T15:01:36.744Z)","checkpoint_updated_ts":"1792001749657"},{"id":"EI-25807214698674439","harness":"papercusp","kind":"bug","title":"improvements:capture agent-review step fails to set status blocked (\"cannot enter status blocked without naming its blocker\"), and dedup coverage silently degraded to unavailable/unavailable","summary":"Two defects observed in the `improvements:capture` result envelope on 2026-10-12, filing EI-25807147914034996 from this session (system:operator/s-1791836612353-4b3d4889, build d740fc3802).\n\n## 1. agent-review block phase fails its own validation\nThe capture returned `reviewRequired: true` alongside:\n\n```\n\"agentReviewFailure\": {\n  \"phase\": \"block\",\n  \"message\": \"work-item EI-25807147914034996 cannot enter status blocked without naming its blocker\",\n  \"at\": \"2026-10-12T20:33:34.717Z\"\n}\n```\n\nThe capture itself succeeded (`ok:true, created:true`), and the item carries `implementationReadiness: { status:\"unknown\", reason:\"awaiting-agent-review\", source:\"capture-policy\" }`. So the review pipeline tried to move the freshly-filed change into `blocked` and was refused by the blocker-naming guard — meaning the post-capture review transition did not complete. The item is left `reviewRequired:true` with readiness `unknown` and no blocker recorded, which looks like a stuck review state rather than a deliberate one.\n\nThis appears structural, not situational: the `block` phase is attempting a state transition without supplying the `blocker` the guard mandates, so it should fail identically for any capture that routes to agent review. Either the block phase should name its blocker (the awaiting-review condition itself is the obvious candidate), or a change awaiting review should not be driven to `blocked` at all.\n\nWorth noting the guard is correct here — a blocked item with no named blocker is exactly the unaccountable-stall shape it exists to prevent. The defect is the caller, not the guard.\n\n## 2. Dedup coverage degraded to fully unavailable, reported only in-band\nSame call returned:\n\n```\n\"dedupCoverage\": { \"lexical\":\"unavailable\", \"semantic\":\"unavailable\", \"degraded\":true },\n\"possibleDuplicates\": []\n```\n\nAn earlier capture from this same session minutes before (EI-25806815274980828, 20:28:16Z) had `{ lexical:\"unavailable\", semantic:\"ok\", degraded:true }`. So semantic dedup went from working to unavailable inside ~5 minutes, and lexical was already down for both.\n\nThe hazard is that `possibleDuplicates: []` reads identically whether dedup ran and found nothing or did not run at all. With both channels unavailable, that empty array carries no information, yet it is the field a filer naturally reads as \"not a duplicate\". This is the bounded-measurement-presented-as-a-verdict shape: the boundedness is disclosed in a sibling field rather than on the result it qualifies. Suggest suppressing or explicitly labelling `possibleDuplicates` when `degraded` is true with no channel `ok`, so an unchecked filing cannot be mistaken for a checked one — and separately investigating why lexical dedup is persistently unavailable on this build.","state":"open","assignee":"su-f0bedfa2-a852-45a8-83ae-df0251ee68c7","updated_ts":"1791905806472","last_progress_at":"2026-10-13 18:26:41.032346+00","source_plan_slug":null,"source_plan_item_ids":null,"claim_hold":null,"needs_owner_action":null,"issue_metadata":{"scope":"harness:papercusp","source":"engineer","severity":"major","created_by":"system:operator/s-1791836612353-4b3d4889","signal_origin":"organic"},"external_blockers":null,"checkpoint":"## Did\nInbox wake rechecked the current lane. Dispatch reservation acceptance-review-target:v1:82e1acb4871cd9ecacb9af9913b5bcfe / WI-6554700010010741.\n\nSymptom: scorecards:emit with all 10 criteria rated was refused with probe_run_failed. Error text: criterion 'r-8' probe was not judgeable (tool_error: read-only probe events:status returned an error: handler_error: events:status — the evidence-only judge may inspect its own awaits only; exact-key inspection and fleet-meter access are unavailable). Nothing was filed (completionReceipt not-recorded).\n\nMechanism, read from source rather than inferred: in packages/operator-core/lib/rubrics-criterion-checks.ts, evaluateCriterionProbeChecks (lines 785-884) plans the probe for every criterion that has a rating (line 795: `input.ratings[c.key] === undefined` is the only skip). It then fails the whole emit closed when any probe result is not fresh or stale (lines 872-884). A complete scorecard must rate r-8, so r-8's probe always runs. That probe's third child is { tool:'events:status', args:{ event:'rubric:criterion-regressed:papercusp-app-performance' }, expect fire_latch.fire_count >= 1 }. It runs under the caller's role envelope, and that is the role designated to grade (the evidence-only judge), which is denied exact-key events:status. So no judge can ever file this rubric's scorecard, regardless of the rating chosen.\n\nThe underlying fact is healthy. I read the same latch through dev:pg_query on harness_shared.event_key_fires: fire_count=5, last fired 15:31:52Z by system:rubric-rescore, before=pass after=fail. Only the probe's read path is denied.\n\nCandidate fixes, cause verified from source but fix untested: (a) let the probe dispatcher run read-only exact-key events:status for the probe evaluator regardless of caller role; it is a read-only platform check. (b) Allow exact-key events:status for the judge role when the key is named by the rubric being graded. (c) Validate at rubric authoring/vetting that every probe tool is executable by the grader role, so a rubric cannot be vetted while ungradeable. Both have fixtureFingerprint=null, and NEITHER carries adequacy.fixtureFree.\n\nRUBRIC TEXT (rubrics:get spec-test-adequacy rev 11, fixture-calibration method): 'an executable binding with neither a fixture fingerprint nor explicit fixture-free attestation is unknown'. The closure declared its late-discovery holder with `const target` and later assigned the discovered inspector object during the SIGUSR1 polling loop. The exact failing statement is that reassignment immediately after the declaration, before signaling or reading the host. Because the wrapper threw first, it did not signal a process, open an inspector, read discovery metadata, or mutate any terminal.\n\nCurrent-HEAD reproduction: repository HEAD is 5957b7e0f93b55073e64c6c1a0773eeb6e2d84dc; it contains no implementation of this transient closure. A current Node reproduction run was: `const target = null; target = { port: 9229 }` => `TypeError: Assignment to constant variable.`; changing the declaration to `let target = null` permits the same assignment and produced `{port:9229}`. This isolates the JavaScript binding error from the terminal-repair source.\n\nAffected path and user impact: only the adopted-successor verification attempt was aborted before it could produce adoption evidence. No host signal/reload, inspector connection, pane change, history reset, or user-terminal mutation occurred. The impact is lost verifier evidence and a misleading failed command, not a product runtime failure.\n\nRecurrence guard: caller wrapper checklist requires a reassigned polling holder to use `let` (or a separate immutable value per iteration); add a preflight caught reproduction before running any host signal. That file sets EMAIL/CALENDAR_AUTH_SECRET, *_APP_URL, *_DATABASE_URL and *_HTTP_PORT, but no EMAIL_PLATFORM_INVOKE_URL (read at email apps/sidecar/src/runtime.ts:83) or the calendar equivalent. /proc/848361/environ and /proc/2601464/environ confirm it. A grading-integrity audit failed one of the six clause cards that WI-10006781 (P-006, live verification) needs before it can close, and I traced the failure to a defect class that affects the whole plan.\ntool-log tail:\n[aged] 27 calls: code_run×7 capability_bash×6 tools_invoke×6 coord_declare-intent×1 coord_whoami×1 dev_pg_query×1 dev_pipeline_position×1 facts_list×1 memory_search×1 tools_find×1 work_items_get×1\ntools_invoke ·\nwork_items_comment ·\ncode_run ×4 ·\ncapability_bash ·\nsearch_fulltext ·\ncapability_bash ·\ncode_run ·\ntools_invoke ·\ncapability_bash ×2 ·\ntools_invoke ·\nsession_request-compaction ·","checkpoint_updated_ts":"1791335483752"},{"id":"WI-10006998","harness":"papercusp","kind":"change","title":"Installer-enabled WSL mirrored mode breaks users' rootful podman 127.0.0.1-published ports: decide the mitigation","summary":"Follow-up of WI-10006715, which measured the root cause. This item is the owner decision on mitigation.\n\n## Context (measured on papercup-vm-win, 2026-10-06)\npapercusp-desktop/src-tauri/src/wsl_setup.rs ensure_wsl_networking_config (WI-3360) writes `[wsl2] networkingMode=mirrored` into the user's GLOBAL %USERPROFILE%\\.wslconfig when no networkingMode is set. Mirrored mode (WSL 2.7.11) installs `table ip filter chain WSLOUTPUT { hook output priority filter; meta mark set 0x1 }`, which overwrites every locally generated packet's mark, plus `ipproto tcp lookup 127` (127.0.0.1 via loopback0) ahead of `lookup local`. Result: in ANY distro, a ROOTFUL podman/netavark `-p 127.0.0.1:<port>` connect from Linux hangs (masquerade mark erased, so the SYN reaches the container from 127.0.0.1); once masquerade is restored, the reply is routed out loopback0 and resets. The same port answers from Windows. Our operator is unaffected (it binds 127.0.0.1 natively). Users' own rootful bridge publishes regress after our installer applies the setting.\n\nVerified workaround (test4, ~/p0-bench/wi10006715/test4.sh): own nft table `out` chain (filter output, priority filter+10) on `ip saddr 127.0.0.0/8 ct status dnat ct direction original` sets ct mark 0x40000 and re-asserts meta mark | 0x2000; `pre` chain (mangle prerouting) copies 0x40000 onto reply packets of ct-marked conns; `ip rule pref 0 fwmark 0x40000/0x40000 lookup local`. Linux side HTTP 200 x3, Windows side still 200, removal restores the hang. A naive `iif podman0 to 127/8 lookup local` rule fixes Linux but BREAKS the Windows side.\n\n## Decision needed (owner)\n(a) Keep auto-mirrored; the cost is now documented in wsl_setup.rs (done in WI-10006715).\n(b) Additionally install the origin-aware workaround from the runtime distro at boot. It modifies the shared WSL netns for all of the user's distros; needs a unit test for the rule rendering and a VM e2e.\n(c) Tell the user at install time that mirrored mode is being enabled, and offer an opt-out.\n(d) Report WSLOUTPUT's mark assignment upstream to microsoft/WSL (related: #13868, #14063). This is outward-facing and needs owner OK.\nAlso: record 'Windows container route uses --network host' as a Decision on plan portable-papercusp-container-and-native-2026-10-06 (draft).\n\nNot measured: Docker Engine in WSL (its OUTPUT DNAT excludes 127/8 and it uses docker-proxy, so it is likely unaffected), rootless podman (rootlessport userspace proxy, likely unaffected), kube-proxy mark-based masquerade (same class, likely affected).","state":"open","assignee":"su-586d69f1-1289-4cd0-824c-09a6f98ee5e7","updated_ts":"1791325836222","last_progress_at":"2026-10-07 01:10:41.618183+00","source_plan_slug":null,"source_plan_item_ids":null,"claim_hold":null,"needs_owner_action":null,"issue_metadata":{"scope":"harness:papercusp","source":"engineer","severity":"minor","created_by":"su-586d69f1-1289-4cd0-824c-09a6f98ee5e7","assigned_by":"su-586d69f1-1289-4cd0-824c-09a6f98ee5e7","signal_origin":"organic"},"external_blockers":null,"checkpoint":"STATE 2026-10-06 22:36Z (su-586d6). Asked Avi 22:33Z via coord:send (askMsgId coord-send-d1e2920d8af7faa0dd863ca3faface562862cf8580515e9c8efc07e5388a75cc). Option (a) is already partly done: the cost is documented in papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/src/wsl_setup.rs (KNOWN COST comment under the WI-3360 section). If he picks (b): the verified rules are in ~/p0-bench/wi10006715/test4.sh (cm_on); implement in the runtime-distro boot path with a unit test of the rendered rules plus a VM e2e that reuses drive.sh/test4 (re-import of p715 takes ~1 min plus ~3 min of apt). (d) is an external publish and needs his explicit OK. The same file passed at f07043ba. Root cause: packages/operator-core/lib/content-lint/shell-syntax.ts findShellSyntaxError catches EVERY execFileSync error, including the 5s timeout (code ETIMEDOUT) and spawn failures, and returns it as a ShellSyntaxError. Its own doc says spawn failures should propagate. Blast radius: the same detector feeds git-sync's content guard (registry.ts shellSyntaxDetector), so under load a clean .sh can be falsely quarantined. Fix: only a bash that ran and exited non-zero yields a verdict; a timeout, spawn error or signal throws ShellSyntaxCheckUnavailableError. The CLI gets a longer per-file timeout and reports unverified files as exit 2 'could not verify', not 'BROKEN'. Make the default to have the global shortcut completely disabled\"\n\nWHY IT MATTERS (the reason #4 is right): a global shortcut is a SYSTEM-WIDE key grab. While registered, the accelerator is taken from every other app on the machine whether or not Papercusp is focused. The old code registered CmdOrCtrl+K unconditionally on first launch — and CmdOrCtrl+K is \"focus search / add link\" in Slack, VS Code, and every browser. So a fresh install silently broke a key the user relies on elsewhere, before they had ever asked for the feature.\n\n== #3 + #4 IMPLEMENTED (su-bf97d, linux leg) ==\npapercusp-desktop/src-tauri/src/docs_search.rs + main.rs:\n- current_shortcut() -> Option<String>; None = DISABLED. DEFAULT_SHORTCUT is DELETED. A key is registered ONLY if a valid preset was explicitly chosen by the user and persisted. Missing file / malformed / explicit null / unknown accelerator => None => OFF. This makes \"off by default\" STRUCTURAL — there is no code path on which a fresh install grabs a key, and no default constant a future caller could fall back to.\n- rebind_shortcut(app,&str) -> set_shortcut(app, Option<&str>); None disables. Registers BEFORE persisting, so a key the OS refuses is never recorded as the active choice (it would come back as a dead shortcut on every launch). Disabling cannot fail.\n- Server tray > \"Docs search shortcut\" > \"Off (no global shortcut)\" is the FIRST item, checked on a fresh install.\n\n== VERIFIED (linux) ==\n- 5/5 docs_search Rust unit tests, incl. disabled_is_the_default_for_every_unchosen_state (every pre-choice file state reads OFF) + off_roundtrips_as_disabled (persists as {\"accelerator\":null}, survives restart).\n- 56 shortcut unit tests green (shortcut-match 21, shortcut-bus 13, dispatcher/help/cheatsheet 22).\n- shortcut-match.ts isMacPlatform() checked: reads the userAgent OS token FIRST because WebKit FREEZES navigator.platform to \"MacIntel\" in webviews — sound, Linux WebKitGTK correctly resolves mod=Ctrl.\n\n== STILL OPEN ==\n- #1 + #2 LIVE on 3 platforms. A specific DB's dump is failing validation: db-backup.sh only renames a dump into place after pg_restore -l passes, so a per-DB 'FAIL' in db-backup.log means the archive was unreadable or the dump errored — read the actual pg_dump error there. DO NOT blindly raise PC_BACKUP_TIMEOUT_SEC without reading it.\n 3. An orphaned pg_dump is holding locks (the EI-10730 knock-on): check for a pg_dump backend older than its timeout (SELECT pid, application_name, backend_start FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE application_name LIKE 'pg_dump%'). db-backup.sh tags its own dumps PGAPPNAME=pcbackup and reaps foreign ones; a lingering 'pg_dump%' backend is a legacy/manual dump.\n 4. A second fixer (spawn ...1792071977216, ~13:46Z) was recorded as release-fixer-no-turn.\n- dev:pipeline_position for packages/operator-core/lib/release/idle-repair-queue-actuator.ts: the OWNER runtime is release-operator at build d740fc3802 with containsChange=false. Leaked scratch dirs are individually tiny — 449,259 of them measured 2.6 GiB total — so every byte-based probe reads this as noise. That was tied to spurious integration-test timeouts and elevated host load fleet-wide (2026-07-09).\n\nDOMINANT NAME SHAPES (random suffixes collapsed — the top line is almost always the culprit):\n   2857 live-fed-gate-snapshot.<rand>\n   1942 papercusp-affected-tests-<n>-<hex>.log\n   1107 prov-sidecar-<rand>\n    739 pc-heavy-start.<rand>\n    432 sidecar-fresh-<rand>\n\nHOW TO ACT ON THIS:\n1. Take the top shape above and find who creates it: grep -rn '<the literal prefix>' --include=*.ts --include=*.mjs --include=*.sh . | grep -v node_modules\n2. Read that creation site's cleanup. If the cleanup is a 'process.on(\"exit\")' handler, IT IS DEAD CODE under vitest: vitest-config.ts pins pool:'forks' and tinypool SIGNAL-KILLS each per-file worker, so Node never runs exit handlers there. Falsify it in both directions before believing either result — run the module under 'tsx -e' (a normal exit, cleanup runs) and under 'npm run test:file' with an isolated TMPDIR (a signal kill, cleanup does not).\n3. The durable fix shape is in libs/test-config/src/hermetic-tmpdir.ts: NEST per-process scratch under one parent so a leak costs the shared TMPDIR one top-level entry, and SWEEP siblings whose creating pid is dead on create. Cleanup that requires the dying process to cooperate is not cleanup — a SIGKILLed process runs nothing.\n4. Reclaiming is safe only with an age floor, so a live run's scratch is never deleted under it: find '/tmp' -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d -name '<shape>*' -mmin +240 -exec rm -rf {} +\n\nWHY BOTH /tmp AND /tmp/pcv ARE WATCHED: vitest-config.ts FORCES TMPDIR=/tmp/pcv for every test process, so a count of /tmp's top level cannot see the directory where test scratch actually lands. Measuring only /tmp under-reported this exact leak by 6x (74,385 seen vs 523,644 real).
